legal.headline: Waste of judicial time: Supreme Court pulls up UP magistrate for 70-page order summoning exonerated accused
legal.hook: Waste of judicial time: Supreme Court pulls up UP magistrate for 70-page order summoning exonerated accused
legal.summary: The Court said the magistrate had written a "dissertation" on police duty while summoning new accused on a protest plea without following CrPC.
legal.contextNote: The Supreme Court, in a bench decision dated 24 Oct 2024, rebuked a Uttar Pradesh magistrate for issuing a 70‑page order that summarily re‑summoned an accused who had already been acquitted by the trial court. The Court held the magistrate had over‑stepped the limits of Section 167 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) by treating the order as a ‘dissertation’ on police duties and by invoking the protest petition without complying with the procedural requisites of CrPC. No prior Supreme Court precedent directly on ‘summoning exonerated accused’ was cited; the decision rests on the principle that once an accused is acquitted, the presumption of innocence prevails and further summons must be grounded in fresh material, not a re‑hash of earlier proceedings.
